title: Functions and graphs
learner: Returning learners who have previously met algebra and graphs but need to recover connected reasoning, representation, and model interpretation.
assumedKnowledge: Signed arithmetic and fractions from F01
Equivalent transformations, interval notation, and root restrictions from F02

include: Coordinate scales, lines, intercepts, and rate units
Function meaning, domain/range, finite data, and piecewise boundaries
Point transformations, graph features, and extrema
Composition, inverse domains, and two-sided verification
Average rates, linear calibration, residuals, and supported predictions
exclude: A complete first course in algebra
Formal limits and differentiation, deferred to F08 and CSC 208
Regression estimation and measurement uncertainty beyond the stated deterministic tasks
Logarithms and periodic functions, reviewed in F04 and F05

routes.quick: Take five diagnostic probes, read the Quick recall section for suggested lessons, then use independent lesson checkpoints and the four-question mixed review. Short-screen success does not certify a whole objective.
routes.full: Follow the five lessons in order, including complete built-in explanations, worked examples, guided work, investigations, practice with hints, and fresh independent checkpoints. Pause the longer source lessons between sections and preserve questions in notes.

escalation.text: Use the complete MTH 215 sequence for first-time instruction or gaps beyond these topics. Return to F01 or F02 when numerical or symbolic operations block function reasoning.

reuse.implementation: Use the F02 adapter and source-version guard. Preserve original source prose, examples, figure descriptions, guided fields, activities, and answer rules; add original refresher framing and independent F03 IDs.
reuse.overlap: B05 provides the coordinate bridge. M02 supplies functions, transformations, composition/inverses, and calibration. F06 later deepens measurement units; F07 develops vector geometry; F08 develops instantaneous rates.

assessment.lessonCheckpoints: Four required questions per lesson. Strengthen source checkpoints with horizontal/vertical distinctions, interior versus absolute extrema, both inverse identities, and average rates over unequal intervals.

mixed.design: First question combines a textual intercept model with a domain problem; remaining questions retain necessary figures or use explicitly separated textual parts. No figure is silently dropped.

assessment.evidence: Confidence, reading, and hints never create independent evidence. Diagnostics and practice guide review. Required lesson checkpoints and mixed recall have separate immutable seeds and snapshots.
assessment.recommendations: Use existing per-family and per-part target mappings. A miss remains a review need until a later independent lesson check.

acceptance: All five full lessons, local prerequisite links, exact readings, original refresher recall, and expanded objective coverage exist.
All source instructions and figures remain intact; source IDs and saved MTH attempts remain unchanged.
New boundary questions independently checked; reused family suites verify domains, graphs, transformations, inverse identities, weighted rates, units, and residuals.
Browser tests cover curriculum entry, diagnostic gap routing, all independent checkpoints, mixed recall, retries, notes, exact resume, backups, mobile, keyboard, and Axe.
Unit tests, lint, typecheck, and production build pass. Record implementer verification separately from independent human review.
Finish F03 before the detailed F04 plan.
